article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: OGKB Blueberry Headband × Grape Gas
Breeder: Compound Genetics
THC Content: 25–30%
CBD Content: Usually below 1%
Terpene Profile: myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Blueberry, sweet grape, berry candy
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: High under favorable conditions
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Some cannabis strains earn attention because of a fashionable name; Glitter Bomb earned its reputation because the flower can look almost unreal under good lighting. The name is unusually literal here: mature buds often appear dusted with a thick, sparkling layer of glandular trichomes that contrasts sharply against the darker flower. Dark violet calyxes, pale resin, flashes of green, and orange pistils give finished buds the jeweled appearance suggested by the name, while the aroma moves in a different direction—ripe blueberry, grape candy, perfume, and sharp fuel. Beneath that visual appeal is a potent, indica-leaning hybrid with enough early mental lift to keep the experience from feeling immediately sleepy.
Genetics and Lineage

Glitter Bomb originates from El Chivo, a Compound Genetics pairing of OGKB Blueberry Headband and Grape Gas. The breeder identifies Glitter Bomb as one of the standout phenotypes selected from that cross rather than a separate seed line with unrelated ancestry. Grape Gas supplies much of the grape sweetness, fuel character, resin production, and modern dessert-gas influence. OGKB Blueberry Headband contributes a deeper berry profile, Kush-like density, darker coloration, and a heavier physical character.

That lineage also helps explain the plant’s distinctive appearance. Well-grown examples can develop thick, closely stacked calyxes beneath a highly visible trichome layer. Purple coloration is common, although environmental conditions and phenotype can shift individual plants toward greener or nearly black-purple flowers. The original El Chivo population was described by Compound Genetics as having longer internodal spacing and clearly separated bud sites, a structure that can improve light penetration and airflow when trained correctly.
Effects and Experience

The first phase is often brighter than the cultivar’s heavy appearance might suggest. A moderate inhalation can produce a quick change in mood, with mental tension easing while music, food, conversation, or visual entertainment becomes more absorbing. Euphoria may arrive alongside a slightly dreamy headspace rather than sharp stimulation. Larger doses can shorten that energetic period, especially for anyone with modest THC tolerance. That dose sensitivity is important because the same flower that feels cheerful and conversational in a small session can become far more sedating when consumed heavily.

As the experience develops, physical relaxation tends to become the defining feature. Muscles may feel loose, movement less urgent, and the desire to remain seated noticeably stronger. The mental side usually stays pleasant but can become hazy at higher amounts, which makes this weed better suited to evenings, movies, gaming, or other situations where intense concentration is unnecessary. Because commercial examples can reach the upper 20% THC range, inexperienced consumers should approach the strain cautiously. Too much may instead produce dizziness, anxiety, or racing thoughts.
Medical Benefits

Glitter Bomb is sometimes chosen by medical cannabis patients looking for a potent cultivar that combines mood elevation with pronounced body relaxation. Its calming character may appeal to adults managing everyday stress, difficulty unwinding, or temporary low mood, while the heavier later phase may be useful for those who prefer marijuana near bedtime. Some consumers also turn to THC-dominant flower for discomfort, muscle tension, or reduced appetite, though these uses are not strain-specific clinical proof.

No controlled clinical evidence demonstrates that this cultivar itself treats a particular medical condition, and its high THC concentration is not ideal for every patient. THC can impair coordination and short-term memory, while larger amounts may worsen anxiety in susceptible people. Anyone using cannabis for a health concern should consider dose, medication interactions, and individual tolerance rather than assuming a popular strain will produce a predictable result.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Breaking apart a cured flower reveals why the genetic pairing works so well. Sweet grape and blueberry usually appear first, sometimes resembling grape syrup, berry candy, or a dark fruit dessert. Once the bud is ground, the fuel side becomes harder to miss. Kerosene, pepper, and earth cut through the fruit, creating a distinctly sweet-gas profile. Compound Genetics describes the parent El Chivo expression with sweet grapes, blueberry, candy, kerosene gas, and subtle perfume, all of which closely match the aromatic identity associated with the Glitter Bomb selection.

The flavor follows a similar sequence but tends to be smoother than the raw aroma. Inhalation can bring blueberry and purple-grape sweetness, followed by candy-like fruit and mild floral tones. On the exhale, peppery spice, earth, and fuel linger longer on the palate. Myrcene and beta-caryophyllene often shape the herbal and spicy dimensions, while limonene and linalool can reinforce fruit and floral impressions; laboratory terpene profiles can vary considerably between cultivators and harvests. For that reason, the aroma of a particular batch is often more informative than a generic terpene chart.
Growing Information

From a cultivation standpoint , Glitter Bomb is comparatively approachable for a premium-looking cultivar. Indoors, topping or gentle low-stress training can encourage several productive branches while preventing a single dominant leader from taking over the light footprint. Flowering generally finishes in about eight to nine weeks, matching Compound Genetics’ specifications for the El Chivo population. Strategic defoliation can help expose interior bud sites, but aggressive stripping is rarely necessary when the plant has been shaped well during vegetative growth. Buds become dense and resinous late in bloom, so adequate air movement and humidity control become increasingly important.

Outdoor plants can become substantial where autumn weather remains dry and mild. Because harvest timing varies with latitude and phenotype, growers should judge ripeness by trichome development and flower maturity rather than the calendar alone, although late September into early October is a reasonable planning window in many temperate locations. With sound environmental control, growers can produce dark, resin-heavy buds without managing an especially temperamental plant. Cool nighttime temperatures late in bloom may deepen purple expression, although coloration depends heavily on genetics and should never be forced by excessively cold conditions.
FAQ
Is Glitter Bomb indica or sativa?

Glitter Bomb is best described as an indica-leaning hybrid. Its early effects can feel upbeat or euphoric, but the experience typically shifts toward stronger physical relaxation as the dose develops. Exact balance can vary by batch, dose, and individual response.
What are the genetics of Glitter Bomb?

The cultivar comes from OGKB Blueberry Headband crossed with Grape Gas. Compound Genetics released the underlying cross as El Chivo, and Glitter Bomb emerged as a particularly notable phenotype selected from that genetic population.
How strong is Glitter Bomb?

It is generally considered a high-potency marijuana strain. Commercial examples frequently fall in the mid-to-upper 20% THC range, although laboratory results differ by grower and harvest. People with low tolerance should start cautiously.
What does Glitter Bomb taste like?
The dominant flavor is usually a combination of blueberry, grape, and sweet berry candy backed by floral notes and pungent gas. The finish can introduce pepper, earth, and kerosene-like sharpness.
How long does Glitter Bomb take to flower?

Indoor flowering is typically about eight to nine weeks. Outdoor harvest generally arrives around early autumn, but climate, latitude, plant health, and phenotype can move the actual harvest date earlier or later.
Final Thoughts on Glitter Bomb

Glitter Bomb represents the modern boutique cannabis style at its best: highly resinous flowers, deep coloration, assertive potency, and an aroma that combines dessert-like fruit with unmistakable fuel. The genetics are straightforward—the cultivar is a selected expression of Compound Genetics’ OGKB Blueberry Headband × Grape Gas cross—but the particular combination of traits is what separates it from countless other purple hybrids.

For experienced consumers, its progression from mental uplift into stronger physical relaxation makes the strain especially well suited to late-day use when productivity is no longer the priority. Growers receive a different set of advantages: manageable structure, an eight-to-nine-week bloom period, impressive resin production, and flower that can develop exceptional visual contrast. It is less suitable for THC-sensitive users or anyone seeking a clear daytime strain, but it delivers the fruit-forward gas, dense frost, and calming finish many experienced cannabis consumers seek.
